# Released major tags

The repository channel workflow uses [Actions-R-Us/actions-tagger v2.0.3](https://github.com/Actions-R-Us/actions-tagger/tree/330ddfac760021349fef7ff62b372f2f691c20fb), pinned to `330ddfac760021349fef7ff62b372f2f691c20fb`.
It runs on a genuine `release: published` event in the canonical repository.
Only non-draft, non-prerelease releases with full `vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` tags enter
promotion. There is no checkout, PHP updater, Composer install, manual recovery
input or substituted GitHub event/context. Editing release notes does not promote.

`prefer_branch_releases: false` creates moving major **tags**: a published 0.x
promotes `v0`; a future 1.x promotes `v1` without moving `v0`. This does not
authorize a major release. `publish_latest_tag: true` also advances the moving `latest` tag to the highest
SemVer release across majors, including 1.x, while `v0` stays on 0.x.
Consumers continue using `@v0` without Dependabot changes. Composer/CPX version
constraints remain independent.

## Activation requires separate approval

This replacement is a review candidate, not an activated automatic path. Do not
merge until publication credentials and channel-name migration are approved and
verified. No credentials, environments, rulesets or refs are changed by this PR.

The current Changelog caller uses `github.token`. GitHub suppresses downstream
release workflows for events generated by that token. Therefore leaving the
publisher unchanged makes automatic channel promotion stop. The published
Changelog lifecycle has no publication-only credential input; its `token` secret
is shared across trusted lifecycle operations. Supplying it globally would expand
credential use beyond publication and is not part of this patch.

The coordinated Changelog patch adds optional `publish-app-client-id`,
`publish-environment` and `publish-app-private-key` routing only to its publication
job. It separates the publisher identity from `automation-actor`, preserving
`github-actions[bot]` as the verified managed PR author. It is not yet a published
contract; this repository must not send these inputs to the current `@v0`.

The concrete follow-up caller delta, after selecting and verifying a compatible
published Changelog revision, is:

```yaml
# Keep the existing PR preparation/check configuration and automation-actor.
# Pin uses to the verified compatible published Changelog revision first.
with:
  publish-app-client-id: ${{ vars.RELEASE_CHANNEL_APP_CLIENT_ID }}
  publish-environment: release-channels
secrets:
  publish-app-private-key: ${{ secrets.app-private-key }}
```

The public client ID must be a repository variable (or approved literal), not an
environment variable read by the caller: that caller has no environment.
The nested publisher selects `release-channels` and consumes the environment
secret named `app-private-key` directly under the proposed upstream contract.
The caller explicitly passes the secret name through the nested workflow chain;
GitHub supplies the environment-scoped value at the job selecting that environment.
[GitHub requires this declaration even for environment-only secrets](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/reuse-automations/reuse-workflows#using-inputs-and-secrets-in-a-reusable-workflow). Code Standards has no
existing secret to rename; approval must establish this exact name/scope once,
without a new permanent alias or a repository-wide private-key secret.

The selected integration uses job-local repository-scoped App authentication only
for publication, then genuine release-event promotion with a separately minted channel App token.
This is a proposed credential choice, not an App requirement imposed by the action.
It needs separate approval for the Code Standards publisher App identity,
installation/repository scope, Contents write and PR read permissions, environment
and secret binding, and refresh/revocation behavior. No App/environment is assumed
to exist here; the Changelog App setup does not authorize reuse in this repository.
No keys have been read. A static short-lived installation token is insufficient.
Human publication is not selected because it would lose automatic publication.

The common channel template matches Changelog: stable-tag guard, a job-local
repository-scoped App token, then the pinned tagger. The Code Standards token is
limited to `php-fast-forward/code-standards`, requests Contents write and Workflows
write, and is revoked after the job. The ambient job token has Contents read.
The channel selects environment `release-channels`, variable
`RELEASE_CHANNEL_APP_CLIENT_ID` and the same single secret `app-private-key`.
These references do not provision or authorize their targets.

Activation must approve the Code Standards App identity/installation and these
channel permissions separately from the publisher's Contents write/PR read.
The publisher preserves PR authorship and receives the App only in its publish
job. The two repositories use the same execution shape; only repository scope
and configured identity differ. No Code Standards installation or permission
state has been inferred from Changelog.

The proposed environment allows main for publication and full tags `v*.*.*` for
the channel. A workflow at a permitted tag can read the environment key. Therefore
restrict full-tag creation to the approved publisher App, and block full-tag
update/deletion without bypass. Moving tags `v0`, `v1` and `latest` require separate
App-only creation/update rules and deletion blocking without bypass; reserve
homonymous branch names after approved migration. These are pending remote
configuration requirements, not protections installed by this PR. If full-tag
creation remains open to other writers, explicitly accept the resulting key
exposure risk instead of claiming workflow-exclusive authority.

Read-only inspection on 2026-10-28 found `refs/heads/v0` at
`d6f4f14cfc018287ef7a748bead4dd3715c5da95`, matching full tag `v0.8.0`,
and no exact `refs/tags/v0`. Recheck this inventory at activation time.

Before activating tag channels, inspect existing `refs/heads/v0` and
`refs/tags/v0` (and future major names), plus `refs/heads/latest` and `refs/tags/latest`. Reserve each channel name so that a branch
and tag cannot shadow one another. An existing branch needs an explicitly approved
migration preserving its exact verified release SHA; this PR never removes or
moves it. Agree rules for moving major tags separately from immutable full-version
tags. No security configuration is inferred from the Changelog repository.

## Guarantees and deliberate differences

The trusted GitHub release event supplies the release tag and `GITHUB_SHA`.
The action promotes that event SHA. It does not independently re-read the live
release, peel/revalidate the full tag or read back the resulting ref.

In tag mode, the action paginates tag refs and compares full SemVer versions in
the same major, refusing an older event when a higher version tag exists. This is
not a complete catalog of stable published releases: unpublished version tags can
block promotion, and equal-version events are accepted. The repository publishes
stable versions only; prerelease scenarios are not a new supported lifecycle.

The non-canceling repository concurrency group serializes this workflow's jobs.
GitHub may replace a pending run; this is not a durable FIFO. Other writers and
live tag/release changes can race it. The upstream mutation uses `force: true`
for moving tags, without an old-OID lease/CAS, ancestry validation or atomic
verification. These are explicit losses from the removed PHP branch updater,
not guarantees provided by the action. Major and latest promotions are separate
API writes without a transaction; a failure can leave a partial result. Name
reservation is an activation gate,
not an action capability. Accept these differences explicitly before merge;
retaining the old helper is the Git rollback if they are unacceptable.

## Verification and recovery

`composer test` retains the shared workflow-identity and packaging contracts and
executes the actual stable-tag Bash guard with accepted and rejected inputs.
`actionlint .github/workflows/*.yml` checks syntax. Offline action qualification
must execute the exact distributed bundle with mocked GitHub API only, including
major isolation and older-event behavior. It does not establish hosted token
permissions, event delivery, remote protections or live promotion success.

For a failed promotion, inspect the release, full tag SHA, channel SHA and job
logs before recovery. Do not introduce workflow_dispatch with fake context, edit
release notes to force execution, or move refs as a test. Any live recovery is a
separately authorized operation.
